The '''1976 Canadian census''' was a detailed enumeration of the [[Canada|Canadian]] population. Census day was June 1, 1976. On that day, Statistics Canada attempted to count every person in Canada. The total population count of Canada was 22,992,604. This was a 6.6% increase over the 1971 census of 21,568,311.<ref>{{cite web |title=1976 Census of Canada. Volume 1, Population, geographic distributions (Federal electoral districts) |url=https://publications.gc.ca/collections/collection_2017/statcan/CS92-801-1976.pdf |website=[[Statistics Canada]] |publisher=Government of Canada |access-date=July 6, 2024 |archive-date=July 24, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170724135526/https://publications.gc.ca/collections/collection_2017/statcan/CS92-801-1976.pdf |url-status=live}}</ref>

The previous census was the [[1971 Canadian census|1971 census]] and the following census was in [[1981 Canadian census|1981 census]].
